newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian state to sell bank's insurance unit.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian state to sell bank's insurance unit.

text.p: Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul state said it plans to privatize the insurance unit of state-owned bank Banrisul and has hired a group of advisors to design a sale model.

"This will be the first insurance company to be privatized in Brazil," state Energy, Mines and Communication Secretary Assis de Souza, head of the state's privatization program, was quoted as saying in a statement.
State officials said they expect to publish bid specifications for the sale of Companhia Uniao de Seguros Gerais in September, once the advisory group completes its work.
No sell-off date or other privatization details were given.

The state on June 5 hired a group made up of Banque Paribas and Banco Fator, auditors Ernst & Young and the Azevedo Sodre law firm to prepare a sale model and financial study of the firm within 90 days.
"The advisor will work keeping in mind foreign investors who have expressed interest in investing in the area of insurance," Souza said.
The Banrisul insurance subsidiary is ranked 16th in Brazil's 11 billion real ($10.2 billion) insurance industry by the National Insurers Federation.
The country's 16 largest insurers hold 68 percent of the country's insurance market, while the remaining 32 percent is spread among some 100 companies.
Rio Grande do Sul accounts for 16 percent of the country's insurance market, the statement said.
